$$
\begin{aligned}Q + R - (Q + P) & =Q+R-Q-P \\  & =\cancel{Q}+R-\cancel{Q}-P \\  & =R-P\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}(A+B)-C-(B-C+D) & =A+B-C-B+C-D \\  & =A+\cancel{B}-\cancel{C}-\cancel{B}+\cancel{C}-D \\  & =A-D\end{aligned}
$$

We are left with a single subtraction. So, we subtract the corresponding entries of the two matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A-D & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 \\ -2 & 5\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-2 & -1 \\ -9 & -5 \\ -9 & 5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}6-(-2) & 6-(-1) \\ 0-(-9) & 4-(-5) \\ -2-(-9) & 5-5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}8 & 7 \\ 9 & 9 \\ 7 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Sum or Difference of Three or More Matrices Using Distributivity

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we simplify the expression by distributing the subtraction over the matrices in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A+B)-C-(B-C+D) & =A+B-C-B+C-D \\  & =A+\cancel{B}-\cancel{C}-\cancel{B}+\cancel{C}-D \\  & =A-D\end{aligned}
$$

We are left with a single subtraction. So, we subtract the corresponding entries of the two matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A-D & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 \\ 8 & -1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -3 \\ -5 & 8 \\ 8 & -3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0-(-5) & 2-(-3) \\ 0-(-5) & -4-8 \\ 8-8 & -1-(-3)\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5 & 5 \\ 5 & -12 \\ 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
